pamphlet_excerpts: Rainy Day Mowing: A rainy day will keep you from mowing the lawn or playing a baseballgame.
Serious Heat Wave: A serious heat wave could prevent your Scout troop from taking ahiking trip.
People Occupations However: For people in some occupations, however, the weather forecast is vital.
Planning Ahead Weather: Planning ahead for weather conditions can mean the difference between profit and loss or even life and death.
step_by_step_procedure: Climate Information Experts: Climate information helps experts lay out airport runways and determine heating and cooling needs for houses, factories.
Climate Records Introduced: Climate records may be introduced as evidence in court to clarifythe causes of accidents on highways, in the air, and at sea.
Climate Canaffect People: Climate canaffect people’s health and social behavior as well as agricultural, commercial, and industrial pursuits the world over.
Pilots Accurate Up-to-date: Pilots need accurate, up-to-date forecasts to help them make decisions such as whether to land a plane.

pamphlet_excerpts: Weather Satellite TIROS-: The first weather satellite, known as TIROS-1, waslaunched in the spring of 1960.
Highly Successfulat: It was highly successfulat giving meteorologists their first overall view of entirestorm systems.
Since Then Satellites: Since then, satellites have become muchmore sophisticated, allowing a nearly continuous watchover the entire Earth.
NOAA has two satellite systems: polar-orbiting satellites and geostationary satellites.
step_by_step_procedure: Satellite Systemsare Named: The satellite systemsare named Polar Operational Environmental Satellites (POES) and Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites.
Polar-orbiting Satellites: The polar-orbiting satellites circle Earth, passingover or near the poles at a height of approximately 520 miles.
Theytravel Globe Several: Theytravel around the globe several times each day.
Polar-orbitingsatellites Placed: The polar-orbitingsatellites are placed in sun-synchronous orbits, which means theypass over the same spot at the same time each day.

pamphlet_excerpts: Meteorologists Main: Meteorologists use four main groupings for clouds: low clouds, middle clouds, high clouds, and clouds that develop vertically.
Meteorologists Consider: Meteorologists also consider the shapes of clouds. clouds are The highest clouds are generally above 20,000 feet and are calledcirrus clouds.
Cirrus Cloudsare Composed: Cirrus cloudsare composed entirely of ice crystals because of their lowtemperatures and the heights where they form.
Cirrocumulus Clouds Arranged: Cirrocumulus clouds can be arranged in patchesor aligned in rows. sometimes called “mare’s tails” because theylook a bit like ahorse’s tail.
step_by_step_procedure: Earth Atmosphere Thought: Earth’s atmosphere can be thought of as an ocean.
Its Restless Movement: Its restless movement is the source of everything people callweather.
Study Atmosphere Its: The study of the atmosphere and its weather is thescience of meteorology.
Components Atmosphere: Components of the Atmosphere The atmosphere is a mixture of gases, six of which are presentin amounts large enough to be important.

pamphlet_excerpts: Thing Weather Moisture: The most important thing about the weather is the moisture itbrings.
Wind Blow Night: The wind could blow night and day and the temperature could rise and fall, but if no rain fell, Earth would be inreal trouble.
Fortunately Addition: Fortunately, in addition to a wonderful air-circulatingsystem, Earth has a wonderful water-circulating system.
Water Vapor Forms: The water vapor that forms clouds and precipitation comes mostlyfrom evaporation from Earth’s oceans.
step_by_step_procedure: Small Part Comes: A small part comes fromlakes, streams, and transpiration, that is, the giving off of waterby the leaves of green plants.
Rain Falls Land: Most of the rain that falls over land evaporates and istransported as water vapor by the winds, often many thousandsof miles from its source.
Water Vapor Condenses: Water vapor condenses (changes from a gas to a liquid) in clouds and falls back to Earth as rain, snow, and other forms of precipitation.

pamphlet_excerpts: Recall Weather Condition: Recall that weather is the condition of the atmosphere over aparticular area for a short time.
Climate Average Theweather: Climate is the average of theweather over a region for a longer time, such as 30 years or more.
Word Climate Comes: The word climate comes from the Greek word klima, meaning “angle.” This name was used because the angle atwhich the sun strikes Earth largely determines.
Equator Sun Nearly: At the equator, the sun is nearly straight overhead most ofthe year, so most of the equatorial region is hot.
step_by_step_procedure: Poleward Equator Theclimate: Poleward from the equator, theclimate gradually shifts from hot to cold.
Tilt Degrees Perpendicular: This tilt (about 23.5 degrees from the perpendicular) remains the same allyear as seen from deep space (top) but changes relative to the sun.
Thesummer Solstice Day: At thesummer solstice (the first day of summer, bottom left), the North Pole tilts toward thesun, and the sun reaches its northernmost point.
Longest Day Ofthe: This is the longest day ofthe year in the Northern Hemisphere.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Make one of the following instruments: wind vane, anemometer, rain gauge, or hygrometer. Keep a daily weather log for one week using information from this instrument as well as from other sources such as local radio and television stations, NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards, and internet sources (with your parent or guardian's permission). Record the following information at the same time every day: wind direction and speed, temperature, precipitation, and types of clouds. Be sure to make a note of any morning dew or frost. In the log, also list the weather forecasts from radio or television at the same time each day and show how the weather really turned out. (b) Visit a National Weather Service office or talk with a local radio or television weathercaster, private meteorologist, local agricultural extension service officer, or university meteorology instructor. Find out what type of weather is most dangerous or damaging to your community. Determine how severe weather and flood warnings reach the homes in your community.

pamphlet_excerpts: Measuring Recording Weather: Measuring and Recording the Weather The most obvious way to study theweather is to observe actual events and keep a record of what you see.
Daily Observationsof: Daily observationsof temperature, wind, pressure, clouds, andrainfall can help you understand how theatmosphere behaves.
Daily Weatherlog Similar: Keep a daily weatherlog, similar to the one shown, for at least aweek.
Possible Record Observations: If possible, record observations for amonth or more.
step_by_step_procedure: Obtain Readings: You can obtain readings from your owninstruments, from local television or radio, and from internet sites devoted to meteorology.
Comparing Readingsfrom Day: By comparing readingsfrom day to day, you can see how the various weather elementschange at your location in response to passing weather.
Dayrecord Based Local: Keep a 30-dayrecord based on local weather forecasts and your own observations.
Record Observations Same: Make and record observations at the same time each day.
